title: Meta’s AI agent has been blocked from using Amazon.com
slides: Meta's AI agent just got blocked from Amazon.com.
The agent was shopping autonomously to test real-world tasks.
Amazon's systems flagged it as a bot, not a human.
This sets a precedent for agent access policies.
Does your agent respect the sites it visits?
thread_text:
1. Amazon Blocks Meta Agent

When tasked with buying a product, the agent was flagged as a bot and denied checkout. No human could complete the purchase on its behalf.

2. Bot Or Human?

Amazon's detection systems identified the agent within seconds. The company hasn't commented on whether this was a deliberate policy or a technical glitch.

3. Real-World Stress Test

The shopping task wasn't a stunt. It was part of a broader effort to see how autonomous agents perform on live websites. Turns out, many sites aren't ready.

4. Precedent For Access

This isn't just about one blocked purchase. It raises a critical question: will every site now need an agent policy? Early signs suggest yes.

5. Check Your Own Agent

Take a prompt on your AI assistant and ask it to complete a simple online action. If it fails, you've just found your first integration gap. Does your agent respect the sites it visits?
